title: Release Rewind: Micro-timeline Editor for Fast Rollbacks
creator: Olivia Chen
description: Goal: Design a compact, glanceable micro-timeline editor (Release Rewind) that lets operators inspect recent rollout segments, scrub to a point in time, and perform fast roll-forward / roll-back actions with a single confirmation. This UI sits on the rollout detail page and complements existing traffic-split editors by focusing on temporal visualization and emergency reversal workflows. Deliverables: Figma proto, accessibility spec, clickthrough prototype, usability test notes, and final handoff spec for frontend + product.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-timeline renders up to 72h of rollout history with segment markers and error/metric overlays
Users can scrub to any segment and preview the affected traffic split before applying rollback/roll-forward
Primary actions: Fast Rollback (immediately revert to previous stable variant) and Soft Rollforward (incremental ramp to a target variant) are accessible within 2 clicks
Confirm dialog includes cost and impact estimates and an undo window for 2 minutes
Design passes a 5-participant usability test with task completion >= 80% and median time-to-rollback <= 45s
user_flows: Flow A: On-call user sees spike in error rate -> open rollout detail -> timeline shows spike overlay -> scrub to pre-spike state -> click Fast Rollback -> confirm -> system rolls back
Flow B: PM wants to accelerate canary -> open timeline -> select canary segment -> choose Soft Rollforward -> set 10% step -> preview and apply
Flow C: Audit: reviewer opens timeline -> expands segment for metadata (actor, commit, runbook link) -> export timeline snapshot
design_decisions: Use a condensed horizontal timeline with heatmap-style metric overlays so operators get signal without losing space for other rollout controls
Show both absolute time and segment-relative offsets to help correlate with external incidents
Primary rollback action is contextual (revert to last stable variant) to reduce selection mistakes; advanced rollback options live in an overflow menu
Preview state is non-destructive and rendered using the same model variant compatibility checks as runtime routing to avoid mismatches
tradeoffs: Compact visualization reduces the amount of metadata shown inline — decision to surface commit/user metadata on hover/expand instead of always visible
Providing an undo window adds operational complexity (state management + observability) but significantly reduces blast radius of mistaken rollbacks
Embedding cost estimates requires integration with billing signals; initial launch will show estimated token-rate delta rather than exact dollar amounts
